content.user_title: Design Reliable APIs with Proven Patterns
content.value_statement: Choosing an API style and consistent conventions requires many connected decisions. This skill provides focused guidance for design, security, evolution, validation, and documentation.
actual_capabilities: Compares REST, GraphQL, tRPC, gRPC, and WebSocket patterns using consumer, data, caching, and platform requirements.
Guides REST resource naming, HTTP method selection, status codes, response formats, and pagination choices.
Recommends authentication, rate limiting, versioning, GraphQL protection, and API documentation practices.
Provides defensive checklists for authentication, authorization, input validation, configuration, and OWASP API risks.
Includes a local validator that reviews up to 15 API source or OpenAPI files for common indicators.
limitations: The guidance does not implement endpoints, schemas, authentication, or infrastructure.
The validator uses simple pattern matching and can produce false positives or miss framework-specific behavior.
YAML validation checks basic text markers and does not fully parse or validate OpenAPI semantics.
Security testing requires explicit authorization and additional environment-specific review.

use_cases.title: Select an API Style
use_cases.description: Compare API approaches against client diversity, data complexity, caching, language, and deployment constraints.

use_cases.title: Standardize Service Contracts
use_cases.description: Define consistent resources, status codes, errors, pagination, authentication, rate limits, and versioning.

use_cases.title: Review API Readiness
use_cases.description: Assess documentation, OpenAPI files, implementation signals, and defensive security controls before release.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an API Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare REST, GraphQL, and tRPC for my project. Ask about consumers, languages, data relationships, caching, and public access before recommending one.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when starting a new API and the architecture is undecided.

prompt_templates.title: Design a REST Contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a REST contract for [domain]. Define resources, methods, status codes, error responses, pagination, authentication, and rate limiting.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when service requirements are known but endpoint conventions are not.

prompt_templates.title: Plan API Evolution
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this API design for compatibility risks. Recommend versioning, deprecation, documentation, and migration practices based on its consumers and release constraints.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when an existing API must change without disrupting clients.

prompt_templates.title: Audit API Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [project path or specification] for design consistency, OpenAPI completeness, authentication, authorization, validation, rate limiting, GraphQL risks, and release blockers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a comprehensive pre-release review with authorized project access.

output_examples.input: Recommend an API style for a public service used by web, mobile, and partner clients.
output: Recommendation: REST with OpenAPI offers broad compatibility and clear client contracts.
Use versioned public routes, cursor pagination, consistent errors, and documented rate limits.
Confirm data complexity and real-time needs before finalizing the design.

output_examples.input: Review pagination for a large, frequently changing transaction dataset.
output: Prefer cursor pagination because offsets can become unstable as records change.
Use a stable sortable field and return an opaque next-page cursor.
Document ordering, page limits, and cursor expiration behavior.

output_examples.input: Create a security review checklist for a new GraphQL API.
output: Verify field-level authorization and restrict production introspection where appropriate.
Set query depth, complexity, and batch limits to control resource consumption.
Test authentication, input handling, rate limits, error exposure, and third-party data trust.

best_practices: Identify consumers, languages, data relationships, and operational constraints before choosing an API style.
Keep response, error, pagination, authentication, and versioning conventions consistent across the service.
Combine automated checks with authorized testing, framework-aware review, and complete documentation.
anti_patterns: Do not default to REST without evaluating consumers, data complexity, and type-safety requirements.
Do not expose internal errors or return inconsistent response structures.
Do not release an API without authentication review, rate limits, documentation, and an evolution plan.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a complete API implementation?
faq.answer: No. It guides design decisions and reviews project files, but implementation remains specific to your framework and environment.

faq.question: When should I choose REST?
faq.answer: Choose REST for public APIs, varied clients, simple resource models, and systems that benefit from standard HTTP caching.

faq.question: When is GraphQL a better fit?
faq.answer: GraphQL fits complex, connected data and multiple clients that need flexible queries, provided the team can manage its security controls.

faq.question: When should I use tRPC?
faq.answer: Use tRPC when TypeScript runs on both ends, clients are controlled, and end-to-end type inference is valuable.

faq.question: What does the validator inspect?
faq.answer: It reads up to 15 matching API source or OpenAPI files and checks for common documentation and implementation indicators.

faq.question: Can the security checklist replace a penetration test?
faq.answer: No. It supports authorized review but does not replace environment-specific testing, threat modeling, or expert assessment.
